info.title: Pathbase API
info.description:
HTTP API for Pathbase — repositories, agent trace paths, computation graphs, and anonymous share links.

**Stability.** v1 endpoints are stable in shape; additive changes (new fields, new endpoints, broader query params) ship without a version bump. Breaking changes get a new prefix (`/api/v2/...`) and a deprecation window.

**Spec format.** OpenAPI 3.1, served live at `/api/v1/openapi.json`.

**Versioning header.** Every response carries an `X-Pathbase-Version` header with the running build's identifier (`<crate-version>+<git-sha>`). The spec does not enumerate it per operation; consumers may read it from any response to pin or correlate.

**Auth.** Most endpoints require a `pat_…` bearer token (see `bearerAuth`). Obtain one through the CLI grant flow (`POST /api/v1/auth/cli/request-grant` then `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/redeem`). Unauthenticated endpoints — the `Anon` namespace, public profile reads — are clearly tagged. Per-operation `security` annotations reflect the actual gate.

post.summary: Redeem a CLI pairing grant for a long-lived bearer token.
post.description:
Second leg of the CLI pairing flow (see
`/api/v1/auth/cli/request-grant` for the full sequence). The CLI
posts the code the user typed; the server normalizes case and
whitespace, consumes the grant, and — on a still-valid grant —
returns the bearer token plus user. Single-use; subsequent
redemptions of the same code return 401.

No authentication is required to call this endpoint; the grant code
IS the authentication. A code that is unknown, expired, or already
redeemed all collapse to `401 Unauthorized` so the response cannot
be used to probe for valid codes — the three failure modes are
deliberately indistinguishable.

requestBody.description: The grant code the user pasted into the CLI. Case and surrounding whitespace are normalized server-side.

200.description: Grant redeemed. Store `token` securely and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent API calls; it is shown only once.

400.description: Code is the wrong length after normalization (must be exactly 8 alphanumeric characters).

401.description: Code is unknown, expired, or has already been redeemed. The three failure modes are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary:
Mint a short-lived grant code for pairing the pathbase CLI to this
browser session.
post.description:
**Pairing flow.**
1. Browser (already authenticated) calls this endpoint and displays
   the returned `code` to the user.
2. User pastes the code into a CLI prompt (`pathbase login`).
3. CLI POSTs the code to `/api/v1/auth/cli/redeem`.
4. Server consumes the grant and returns `{ token, user }` to the
   CLI.
5. CLI stores `token` and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer
   <token>` on every subsequent API call.

The grant is single-use and expires after a short window. Multiple
grants may be active concurrently; redeeming one has no effect on
existing tokens.

200.description: Grant issued. Display `code` to the user so they can paste it into the CLI before `expires_in` seconds elapse.

401.description: Caller is not authenticated. Grants can only be minted by an already-logged-in browser session.

get.summary: List the authenticated user's active sessions.
get.description:
Returns one entry per session owned by the caller — both browser
logins and CLI tokens. Includes an `is_current` flag so the UI can
mark which entry is the caller's own session.

Used by the settings UI to render "active devices/CLIs" with a
per-entry revoke button (which calls
`DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/{id}`).

200.description: All active sessions for the current user, including the one that issued this request (marked with `is_current: true`).

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller's sessions.
delete.description:
Ends the session identified by `{id}`, immediately invalidating
its token. The caller can revoke any of their own sessions,
including the one that issued this request — doing so will end
the current login. Sessions belonging to other users are reported
as `404 Not Found` (no leakage of "exists but isn't yours").

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the session to revoke. Obtain from `GET /api/v1/auth/sessions`. Revoking your current session ends the request's own login.

204.description: Session revoked. The associated token is no longer accepted.

404.description: No session with this ID exists, or it belongs to another user. The two cases are deliberately conflated.

post.summary:
Upload a graph anonymously as the `anon` user. No authentication
required; the resulting graph is always `Unlisted` and reachable
only via the returned share URL.

requestBody.description: Toolpath Graph document. The body's `visibility` field is ignored; anon uploads are always `Unlisted`.

201.description: Graph stored; the `url` in the response is the share link.

400.description: Document failed to parse as a toolpath Graph.

get.summary: Return the authenticated user's full profile.
get.description:
Canonical "who am I?" endpoint. Returns the user matching the
caller's bearer token. The returned shape matches the public
`GET /api/v1/u/{username}` response with one difference: `email`
is included here because the caller is reading their own profile.

200.description: The authenticated user, including the private `email` field.

put.summary: Replace the authenticated user's editable profile fields.
put.description:
PUT semantics: the body is the new state. Fields not present
(or `null`) are cleared. Username, email, and avatar are not
editable here. Returns the updated user.

requestBody.description: Complete new state of the editable profile fields. Missing or `null` clears the field — send the current value to preserve it.

200.description: Profile updated; returns the post-update user.

get.summary:
List repositories owned by `{owner}`. The DB layer applies the
visibility filter in SQL using the resolved `Viewer`: owners get
all three states (Public + Unlisted + Private); non-owners get
`Public` only. There is no caller-side branching, and no helper
that returns "everything" without a viewer.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional. Server-bounded; out-of-range values are clamped silently.

200.description: Owner's repositories. Owners see all repos; other viewers see only public repos.

post.summary: Create a new repository owned by the authenticated user.
post.description:
The new repo's owner is taken from the session — there is no way
to create a repo on behalf of someone else through this endpoint.
(Owner usernames in URLs are read-only metadata; ownership is set
once at creation.) The repo defaults to public visibility.

Returns the created `Repo` with its server-assigned UUID and
timestamps.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username

requestBody.description: Name and optional description for the new repo. Owner is implicit (the authenticated user).

example.description: Captured runs of my coding agent.
example.name: agent-traces

201.description: Repository created. Body is the new `Repo`.

401.description: Not authorized to create under this owner.

409.description: An owner already has a repo with this `name`. Names are unique per owner.

get.description:
Public read; no authentication required. Returns the `Repo`
including description, README, visibility flag, and timestamps. To
list a repo's paths or graphs, follow up with the corresponding
`/paths` and `/graphs` collection endpoints.

**Reserved owners.** `me` and `anon` are reserved namespaces; this
endpoint returns 404 for either. Use `/api/v1/anon/...` for
anonymous content and `/api/v1/u/me` (and `/api/v1/u/{owner}/repos`) for
the calling user's own resources.

**Visibility.** `can_read` is enforced: `Public` returns to anyone,
`Unlisted` (system-managed; URL-addressable) returns to anyone,
`Private` returns only to the owner — others get `404`. Repos are
addressed by guessable name, so there's no share-by-link at this
level for `Private` repos. (Per-graph/per-path share-by-link inside
`Public` repos is unaffected — those still gate on their own
visibility.)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username. The reserved values `me` and `anon` always 404.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name (unique per owner).

404.description: Owner unknown, repo unknown for that owner, repo is secret and the viewer is not the owner, or owner is a reserved namespace (`me`, `anon`).

put.summary: Replace a repository's editable fields (name, description, README).
put.description:
Owner-only: the authenticated user must match `{owner}`. Reserved
owners (`me`, `anon`) always return 404.

PUT semantics: the body is the new state. To preserve any field,
send its current value; missing or `null` clears the nullable
fields. Visibility is changed through the separate `/visibility`
sub-resource. Renaming changes the canonical URL of the repo (and
every nested resource), so callers should expect old links to 404
afterward.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username; must match the authenticated user. `me`/`anon` always 404.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name (current — pre-rename).

requestBody.description: Complete new state of the editable repo fields. `name` is required; missing/`null` clears `description` and `readme`. Send back the current values to preserve them.

example.description: Captured runs of my coding agent (now with vendor labels).
example.name: agent-traces

401.description: Not authenticated, or the caller is not the owner.

404.description: Owner unknown, repo unknown, or owner is a reserved namespace (`me`, `anon`).

409.description: Renaming to a name already used by another of this owner's repos.

delete.summary: Delete a repository and all its contents.
delete.description:
Owner-only. Removes the repo and all paths and graphs in it.
Irreversible. Reserved owners (`me`, `anon`) always return 404.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username; must match the authenticated user. `me`/`anon` always 404.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name.

204.description: Repository (and all paths and graphs in it) deleted.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the caller is not the owner.

404.description: Owner unknown, repo unknown, or owner is a reserved namespace (`me`, `anon`).

get.description:
Returns up to `?limit=` graphs under `{owner}/{repo}`, ordered by
creation time. The DB layer applies the visibility filter in SQL
using the resolved `Viewer`: the owner sees all three states
(`Public` + `Unlisted` + `Private`) so the UI can render the
`unlisted` pill and offer a show/hide toggle; everyone else sees
only `Public`. Non-public graphs remain reachable by direct UUID
share-link regardless of listing visibility.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Username of the repository's owner.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name within the owner's namespace.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional. Server-bounded; out-of-range values are clamped silently.

200.description: Page of graphs in the repository, capped by `?limit=`. Each entry carries the graph row plus `path_count` and the `url` clients should link to. Owners see all graphs; other viewers see only public graphs.

404.description: Owner unknown, repo unknown for that owner, or owner is a reserved namespace (`me`, `anon`).

post.summary: Create a graph from a multi-path toolpath document.
post.description:
Inline path entries (`PathOrRef::Path`) are admitted into the same
workspace as the graph (deduped by toolpath ID; an existing match
is linked rather than re-created). Refs to existing paths
(`PathOrRef::Ref`) are kept as ID references and not re-stored.

Caller must own `{owner}/{repo}`. The `document` field must parse
as a `toolpath::v1::Graph`.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Username of the repository's owner. Must match the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name within the owner's namespace.

requestBody.description: Multi-path toolpath Graph document, optional display name, and visibility (`public`/`unlisted`/`private`, default `unlisted`). Inline paths are admitted into the workspace; refs are kept as ID references.

201.description: The newly created graph with its server-assigned UUID, the reconstructed multi-path `document`, and the canonical `url`.

400.description: Document failed to parse as a toolpath Graph.

401.description: Missing/invalid bearer token, or the authenticated user does not own the target repository.

get.summary:
Fetch a single graph with its full reconstructed multi-path
document. `Public` and `Unlisted` graphs are readable by anyone
(possession of the UUID is the share token for `Unlisted`);
`Private` graphs require the caller to authenticate as the owner.
Non-owner reads of a `Private` graph return `404` — same response as
"doesn't exist" so the gate doesn't leak existence.
get.description:
Responses carry an `ETag`; conditional requests using
`If-None-Match` return `304 Not Modified` when the representation
is unchanged.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Username of the repository's owner.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name within the owner's namespace.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Graph UUID. For `Unlisted` graphs the UUID is the share token; `Private` graphs additionally require owner authentication.

200.description: The graph row, its `path_count`, the reconstructed multi-path `document`, and the canonical `url`.

404.description: Owner, repository, or graph not found — or graph is `Private` and the caller isn't the owner.

delete.summary:
Delete a graph. Owner only — knowing the UUID is enough to *read*
(it's the share token) but not enough to mutate.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username — must match the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Graph UUID.

204.description: Graph deleted; constituent paths remain in the workspace.

get.summary:
Stream the graph's reconstructed Graph document as raw JSON — the
inverse of `POST .../graphs`. `Public` and `Unlisted` graphs
download for anyone with the UUID; `Private` graphs require owner
authentication and 404 for everyone else (mirrors "doesn't exist").

200.description: Toolpath Graph JSON file download. Send the returned `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` on a subsequent request to receive 304 when unchanged.

Content-Disposition.description: `attachment; filename="…"`. Filename derives from the graph's display `name` when set, otherwise the graph UUID.

ETag.description: Strong ETag for conditional GETs. Echo as `If-None-Match` on subsequent requests.

404.description: Owner, repository, or graph not found — or graph is `Private` and the caller isn't the owner.

get.summary:
List the paths that belong to a graph, in graph-defined order.
If the parent graph is readable to the caller (`Public`/`Unlisted`,
or `Private` for the owner), all of its constituent paths are
returned; the parent's UUID is the share token. A `Private` graph
404s for non-owners — same as the per-graph GET.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional. Server-bounded; out-of-range values are clamped silently.

200.description: Page of constituent paths in graph-defined order. Each entry carries the path row, `step_count`, and the `url` clients should link to.

get.summary:
Fetch a constituent path with its full reconstructed document.
Conditional via `If-None-Match`.

200.description: Path row plus `step_count`, the reconstructed Graph `document`, and the canonical `url`.

delete.summary:
Delete a constituent path. Owner only. Cascades to its step rows
AND removes the junction row from this graph.

patch.summary:
Patch a constituent path's mutable fields — currently just
`visibility`. Owner only.

200.description: Path updated; returns the path row plus its canonical `url`. Re-fetch the path's full document via the GET endpoint when needed.

get.summary:
Render the path's HEAD-ancestor chain as a chat-projection — a
densely-indexed, pre-classified, optionally pre-rendered
transcript.

parameters.name: include_html
parameters.description:
Render `text` and `thinking` fields to sanitized HTML
server-side. Defaults to true; set false for lighter payloads
when the client renders markdown lazily.

patch.summary: Toggle a graph's public/secret visibility. Owner only.

200.description: Visibility updated; returns the graph row plus its canonical `url`.

patch.summary:
Flip a repo's visibility between `public` and `private`. The
`unlisted` state is system-only — owner cannot set it, and any
repo currently `unlisted` (e.g., the seeded `pathstash`) is locked.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owner username; must match the authenticated user. `me`/`anon` always 404.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name.

requestBody.description: New visibility. Repos accept `public` or `private` only — `unlisted` is system-only.

400.description: Body contained `unlisted`, which is not accepted on repos.

401.description: Not authenticated, or the caller is not the owner.

403.description: Repo's current visibility is `Unlisted` (system-pinned); user cannot modify.

404.description: Owner unknown, repo unknown, or owner is reserved.

get.summary: Look up a user's public profile by username.
get.description:
No authentication required. Returns the same `User` shape as
`/u/me` with one guarantee: `email` is always `null` here — that
field is only ever populated for the caller's own profile via
`GET /api/v1/u/me`.

**Reserved namespaces.** The literal usernames `me` and `anon` are
reserved and always return 404 from this endpoint. Use
`GET /api/v1/u/me` for the calling user and `/api/v1/u/anon/...`
for anonymous content.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Public username. Lowercase ASCII alphanumerics with `-`/`_`. The reserved values `me` and `anon` always 404 here — use `/api/v1/u/me` and `/api/v1/anon/...` respectively.

200.description: Public user profile. `email` is always null here; use `/api/v1/u/me` to read your own email.

404.description: No user with that username, or the username is a reserved namespace (`me`, `anon`).

ActorView.description:
Resolved actor identity for a turn. Lookup happens once on the
server against the document's `meta.actors` block; turns reference
the actor by `u32` index into the projection's `actors` array.

display.description:
Display name resolved against `meta.actors` if present, else the
suffix after `:`.

ApiErrorCode.description:
Closed set of error codes the API can emit. Renders as a snake_case
string on the wire (`not_found`, `unauthorized`, …) and is declared
as an OpenAPI enum so generated clients can switch on it
exhaustively. Add a variant here, never a free-form string in
[`ApiErrorResponse::code`].

ApiErrorResponse.description:
Standard error response envelope for all 4xx/5xx responses.

Every non-2xx response from the API has this shape. The `code`
is a short, stable token from a closed enum suitable for
programmatic dispatch; the `error` is a human-readable message
suitable for log/UI display.

code.description:
Stable token identifying the error class. Clients should
branch on this rather than parsing `error`.

error.description:
Human-readable error message. Suitable for log/UI display; do
not parse for branching.

inserted.description: Number of steps newly inserted (existing `step_id`s are skipped).

path.description: The path's full HATEOAS-decorated document after the append.

ChatCursor.description:
Pagination cursor for fetching older turns. Reserved for future
`?before=<step_id>` requests; currently every projection returns the
full chain in one shot.

before.description:
Canonical step ID one step older than `turns[0]`. `None` when the
chain reaches a root step in this projection.

ChatProjection.description:
Top-level chat-projection response. Densely-indexed (`u32` IDs into
`turns` / `actors`) so JSON parsing is cheap and the wire shape
avoids duplicating actor strings on every turn.

head.description:
Index into `turns` — the latest turn along the HEAD chain. `None`
when the document has no head.

step_ids.description:
Canonical step IDs parallel to `turns`, for deep-links and
`/step/{id}` fetches.

ChatTurn.description:
One linearized turn along the HEAD-ancestor chain. Already
classified, optionally pre-rendered to HTML, with tool invocations
inlined — the renderer drops in `text_html` and renders no further.

invocations.description: `tool.invoke` siblings of an assistant step, spliced inline.

parent_id.description: Index into `turns` — `i - 1` along the HEAD chain, `None` at the root.

text_html.description:
Sanitized HTML for `text`. Empty when `include_html` is false or
`text` is empty.

tool_diff.description:
For `kind = "tool"` only: the first non-empty `change[k].raw`,
pre-split into lines.

ChatTurnKind.description:
Pre-classified turn kind. Server-side classification follows the
precedence rules in `packages/frontend/src/classify.ts`; the client
renders verbatim without re-deriving.

CliGrantResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/request-grant`.

Carries the human-typeable grant `code` that the user pastes into
the pathbase CLI, plus its lifetime. Display the code prominently
in the UI; do not store it in the URL or log files.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the grant in seconds, set by the server.

CreateRepoBody.description:
Request body for `POST /api/v1/u/{owner}/repos`.

Creates a repository owned by the authenticated user. The (owner,
name) pair must be unique; collisions return 409.

description.description:
Optional short description shown next to the repo name in
listings. Free-form; no length cap.

name.description:
Repository name. Must be unique among the authenticated user's
existing repos. Used as the URL slug at
`/api/v1/u/{owner}/repos/{repo}`.

visibility.description:
Initial visibility. Defaults to `public` if omitted. The
`unlisted` state is not accepted on repos — it's reserved for
the system-managed pathstash repo and seeded directly in the DB.

Graph.description:
A computation graph — a named ordered collection of paths within
a repo. Pure storage shape — the columns on `graphs`. Derived
properties (path count, reconstructed document) live on the response
wrappers that need them (`GraphSummary`, `GraphDocument`).

header.description:
Graph metadata: `{graph: GraphIdentity, meta?: GraphMeta}` —
the toolpath `Graph` shape minus its `paths`. Absent when not set.

name.description:
Optional human-readable label for display. Free-form; no URL
implications — graphs are addressed by `id` (UUID) at the wire
boundary. Defaults from the uploader (filename or caller-
provided) and can be edited.

visibility.description:
Visibility — `Public` is listed and world-readable; `Unlisted`
is link-share (UUID grants read); `Private` is owner-only.

GraphDocumentResponse.description:
Wraps a `Graph` with its path count, reconstructed multi-path
document, and the URL. Used by endpoints that promise the full
document on the wire.

GraphResponse.description: `Graph` plus the absolute URL clients should link to.

path_count.description: Number of constituent paths in this graph.

GraphSummaryResponse.description:
Wraps a `Graph` with its path count plus the URL. Used by listing
endpoints.

RedeemBody.description:
Request body for `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/redeem`.

Carries the grant code that the user pasted from the browser into
the CLI. Whitespace and case-folding are tolerated server-side.

code.description:
The grant code displayed by the browser. Whitespace, dashes,
and case differences are normalized away (server uppercases and
strips non-alphanumerics) before lookup; submit it however the
user typed it.

RedeemResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/v1/auth/cli/redeem`.

Returns the new bearer token plus the authenticated user. The token
is shown to the API ONCE; pathbase cannot recover the plaintext if
it is lost.

token.description:
Opaque session bearer token, prefixed `pat_…`. Send as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent API calls. Treat
as a secret; only its hash is retained server-side, so it
cannot be re-shown if lost — the user must re-pair the CLI.

user.description: The user the CLI is now authenticated as.

Repo.description:
A repository — a named workspace of paths and graphs owned by a
single user. `name` is unique per owner and serves as the URL
segment in `/{owner}/{name}` and nested resources.

visibility.description:
Repository visibility. See `Visibility` for the state semantics.
Repos are user-controllable as `Public`/`Private`; `Unlisted`
is system-set (e.g., the seeded `pathstash` repo).

RepoVisibilityInput.description:
Write-side narrowing of [`pathbase_core::Visibility`] for repo
bodies. The repo *read* shape (`Repo.visibility`) still uses the
full three-state enum — a `GET` on the seeded `pathstash` repo
returns `"unlisted"` like always. This type only constrains what
the API will *accept* from a client: `Unlisted` is system-pinned,
users can't enter or leave it through the API, so it doesn't
appear in `POST /repos` or `PATCH .../visibility` bodies.
Generated clients see only `public | private` on inputs and the
`Unlisted` write is unreachable by construction. Graph and path
bodies use the full `Visibility` enum; all three values are legal
there.

SessionSummary.description:
One entry of the session list returned by `GET /api/v1/auth/sessions`.

A session is the durable side of an authentication: one entry
exists for every browser login (`kind = "web"`) and every redeemed
CLI grant (`kind = "cli"`). Sessions can be inspected and revoked
from the user's settings UI.

expires_at.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp at which the session token stops being
accepted.

id.description:
Stable session ID. Use this with
`DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/{id}` to revoke.

is_current.description:
`true` if this entry corresponds to the session that issued
the current request — useful for the UI to mark the "this
device" entry and warn before revoking it.

kind.description:
`"web"` for browser logins (password, GitHub OAuth, dev login),
`"cli"` for CLI tokens minted via `/api/v1/auth/cli/redeem`.

user_agent.description:
`User-Agent` header captured at session creation. Useful for
"is that you on Firefox?" recognition. May be absent for
clients that omit the header.

ToolDiff.description:
Pre-split diff payload — picked from the first non-empty
`change[k].raw` on a structural step. Lines are pre-split so the
renderer doesn't repeat the work.

ToolInvocation.description:
A `tool.invoke` step spliced inline next to its parent assistant
turn. Saves the client a second pass over the path's step graph.

input.description:
Tool input args from the structural payload (`extra.input`),
JSON-stringified when not already a string.

result.description:
Tool output from the structural payload (`extra.result`),
JSON-stringified when not already a string.

step_id.description: Canonical step ID of the tool.invoke step.

ToolpathDocument.description:
A toolpath v1 Graph document. See <https://github.com/empathic/toolpath>
for the full schema; the wire format is JSON with top-level fields
`graph`, `paths`, and optional `meta`.

This is a marker schema used to generate an OpenAPI reference. The
canonical Rust type is `toolpath::v1::Graph` from an external crate
that does not derive `utoipa::ToSchema`, so we describe the shape
with `serde_json::Value`-typed fields here. Generated clients will
see a permissive object shape; they should defer real validation
to the toolpath crate.

meta.description:
Optional document metadata (title, description). Free-form
object; clients should defer real validation to the toolpath
crate.

TracePath.description:
A single agent trace path within a repo. Pure storage shape — the
columns on `paths`. Derived properties (step count, reconstructed
document) live on the response wrappers that need them
(`TracePathSummary`, `TracePathDocument`).

header.description:
Path metadata: `{path: PathIdentity, meta?: PathMeta}` — the
toolpath `Path` shape minus its `steps`. Absent when not set.

name.description:
Optional human-readable label for display. Free-form; no URL
implications — paths are addressed by `id` (UUID) at the wire
boundary. Defaults from the uploader (filename or caller-
provided) and can be edited.

visibility.description:
Visibility — `Public` is listed and world-readable; `Unlisted`
is link-share (UUID grants read); `Private` is owner-only.

TracePathDocumentResponse.description:
Wraps a `TracePath` with its step count, reconstructed Graph
document, and the URL. Used by endpoints that promise the full
document (single-path GET, append-steps response).

url.description:
Absolute URL for this path's web page. UUID-addressed: works
regardless of visibility (knowing the UUID is the share
token for secret resources).

TracePathResponse.description: `TracePath` plus the absolute URL clients should link to.

step_count.description: Number of steps in this path.

TracePathSummaryResponse.description:
Wraps a `TracePath` with its step count plus the URL. Used by
listing endpoints and any single-row reads that surface the count.

visibility.description:
New graph visibility. `public` lists in feeds and is anonymously
readable; `unlisted` hides from listings but stays reachable via
the UUID share link; `private` restricts read to the owner.

UpdateProfileBody.description:
Body for `PUT /api/v1/u/me`.

Carries the complete replacement state of the editable profile
fields. PUT semantics: the body IS the new value — fields not
present (or set to `null`) are cleared. To preserve an existing
value, send it back. Read the current values from `GET /u/me`.

Username, email, and avatar are NOT editable here — username is
immutable, email is bound to the auth provider, and avatar comes
from the OAuth provider's profile.

bio.description:
Free-form short biography rendered on the user's public
profile. Missing or `null` clears the field. No length cap is
enforced at the API layer; expect Markdown but no rendering
guarantees.

display_name.description:
Human-readable display name shown next to the username on
profile pages and trace headers. Missing or `null` clears the
field (the UI then falls back to the bare username).

UpdateRepoBody.description:
Request body for `PUT /api/v1/u/{owner}/repos/{repo}`.

Carries the complete replacement state of the editable repo
fields. PUT semantics: every field is written. To preserve an
existing value, send it back; missing or `null` for the nullable
fields clears them. Read the current state from `GET /repos/{repo}`
first if the form doesn't already have it.

Visibility is NOT editable here — it lives at the sub-resource
`/repos/{repo}/visibility` for two reasons: (1) it's a single
well-defined op clients flip independently of content edits, and
(2) `Unlisted` is system-only and that gate is cleaner to enforce
on its own endpoint.

description.description: New description. Missing or `null` clears the field.

name.description:
New repository name. Required (the column is non-nullable —
there is no "no name" state). Renames must be unique among
this owner's repos (409 on collision). Renaming changes the
URL of the repo and every nested resource — clients holding
old URLs will 404 afterward.

readme.description:
New README body (free-form text/Markdown). Missing or `null`
clears the field. No length cap is enforced at the API layer.

UploadGraphBody.description:
Request body for `POST /api/v1/u/{owner}/repos/{repo}/graphs`.

The `document` field carries a multi-path toolpath Graph; inline
path entries are admitted into the workspace and deduped by their
toolpath ID, refs are kept as ID references.

document.description:
The toolpath v1 Graph document with one or more `PathOrRef`
entries. Inline paths are admitted into the same workspace as
the graph; refs are kept as ID references to existing paths.

name.description:
Optional human-readable display label. Free-form; no URL or
uniqueness implications — the server addresses the created
graph by its UUID `id` in the response. Defaults to whatever
the uploader (web/CLI) chose to send, typically the filename.

visibility.description:
Graph visibility. Omitted defaults to `unlisted` —
reachable only via the graph's UUID share link or to the
authenticated owner. Flip later via `PATCH
/graphs/{id}/visibility`.

User.description:
A registered Pathbase account. `email` is optional because GitHub
OAuth users can have a private email; CLI / API consumers see the
caller's own email via `/u/me` but never another user's.

email.description:
Caller's own email. Populated only by `GET /api/v1/u/me` (the
authenticated self-read). The public profile endpoint
`GET /api/v1/u/{username}` always returns `null` here; emails
are never exposed across users.

Visibility.description:
The visibility state of a `Repo`, `TracePath`, or `Graph`. Used uniformly
across the three entities at the storage and wire layers.

- `Public`: appears in public and owner listings, readable by anyone.
- `Unlisted`: hidden from default listings (even from the owner), but
  readable by anyone in possession of the resource's URL/ID. The
  resource ID is the access gate — for paths/graphs that's the UUID;
  for repos it's a system-pinned state used by `pathstash` only.
- `Private`: hidden from public listings, listed only to the owner,
  readable only by the owner.

bearerAuth.description: Pathbase personal access token (`pat_…`) obtained via the CLI grant flow (`POST /auth/cli/request-grant` then `POST /auth/cli/redeem`). Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

tags.name: Auth: CLI
tags.description: CLI pairing — request a short-lived grant code and redeem it for a `pat_…` bearer token.

tags.name: Auth: Sessions
tags.description: Inspect and revoke the caller's active sessions (browser logins and CLI tokens).

tags.name: Graphs
tags.description: Computation graphs and their constituent trace paths.

tags.name: Anon
tags.description: Unauthenticated share-by-link uploads under the `anon` user. Always `Unlisted`.
